bug: A useState hook (refetching) is declared after an early 'if (loading || !trip) return' in the component, so hook count changes between renders and the page crashes (rules of hooks).
The service worker serves /api/items with StaleWhileRevalidate, so a refetch right after a mutation returns the pre-mutation cached list and the change does not show until reopen.

A style's flat allowedTipos whitelist is applied to every garment of every kind, so tagging a kind with a tipo outside the list (list written for another kind) silently drops those garments from the style and suggestions come back empty.
The refactor collapses the empty-day branch to a bare 'register a look' button and removes the inline DaySuggestions path, so empty past/today days lose their outfit suggestions (regression).

Container assignment merges 'learned' category-to-container memory derived from this trip's own moves, so moving one garment teaches the category and auto-distribute moves every other garment of that category into the same container in the same render.

detectCrossAccountTransfers links a transfer using others.find(), which takes the first compatible row; with two same-amount candidates in the window it links an arbitrary leg with no ambiguity signal, silently removing both rows from income/expense and budgets.

On pathname === '/login' the effect returns early without clearing locked, and LockGuard sits in the root layout so state survives client navigation: the fixed full-screen overlay stays on top of the login form and the password cannot be typed.

The effect that resyncs the segment depends only on initialView; when the pivot drill-down navigates to ?view=lista&category=... from a state where initialView was already 'lista', the effect never fires and the user keeps seeing the pivot while the filter was applied silently.

The outlier 'ok' action only adds to client state so the item returns on reload, and opening an outlier navigates to /transactions?focus=<id>, a parameter the transactions page ignores, so the user lands on the bare list.

The service worker page cache is a fixed name (recall-pages-v1) never invalidated on deploy, so the network-first fallback can serve cached HTML that references chunk hashes the new build no longer serves (stale or blank page).

cron.schedule is created without missedExecutionTolerance; node-cron 4.x silently drops any tick that fires later than its 1 s default, and host timers here run tens of seconds late, so the daily 08:00 nudge is skipped.

startSession inserts a new workout_sessions row on every call with no check for an unfinished session, so a double tap, second tab or retry stacks duplicate running sessions (and Discard then reveals the next one underneath).
